name: Apollo 16 Lunar Rover
summary: The second Lunar Roving Vehicle driven by astronauts, parked in the Descartes Highlands after three moonwalks in April 1972.
discoveries: Carried John Young and Charles Duke to craters and mountain slopes in the Descartes Highlands.
Drove about 26.7 km over three moonwalks.

stories.kids: I’m the second car astronauts ever drove on the Moon. John Young and Charles Duke used me to explore the Descartes Highlands, a rugged land of craters and mountains. When they flew home, they parked me. I’m still parked there.
stories.explorer: Apollo 16 landed in the Descartes Highlands on April 21, 1972. The crew drove their Lunar Roving Vehicle to Stone Mountain and North Ray Crater, covering 26.7 km in all. After the last moonwalk it was left behind, like the rovers of Apollo 15 and 17.
stories.scientist: The Apollo 16 Lunar Roving Vehicle, the second flown, was deployed on the first moonwalk, 21 April 1972 UTC, near 8.97° S, 15.50° E in the Descartes Highlands. Across three moonwalks it covered about 26.7 km (NASA NSSDCA), reaching the slopes of Stone Mountain and the rim of North Ray Crater, and was left on the surface.

image.alt: An Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle parked on the Moon, with its dish antenna and wire wheels, under a black sky.

clues.explain: NASA records about 26.7 km over three moonwalks.

options: I drove away on my own

timeline.title: Landing at Descartes
timeline.text: Apollo 16 lands in the Descartes Highlands, and the crew unpacks and first drives the second Lunar Roving Vehicle.

timeline.title: Up Stone Mountain
timeline.text: On the second moonwalk the rover carries the crew up the slope of Stone Mountain.

timeline.title: Parked for good
timeline.text: After a final drive to North Ray Crater the crew flies home and leaves the rover parked. About 26.7 km driven in all.

learn.title: Who I am
learn.text: I’m the Lunar Roving Vehicle from Apollo 16, the second rover astronauts ever drove on the Moon. John Young and Charles Duke landed in the Descartes Highlands on April 21, 1972.

learn.title: What I did
learn.text: On three moonwalks I carried the crew up Stone Mountain and on to North Ray Crater. In all I drove about 26.7 km.

learn.title: Where I am now
learn.text: After the last moonwalk on April 23, 1972, the crew flew home and left me parked on the Moon. I’m one of three rovers still there, with the rovers of Apollo 15 and 17.
